questions: What does "sound" mean beyond the four listed conditions -- are there implicit requirements not stated?
Should the "more than three digits" check count digits anywhere in the filename, including the extension?
Must there be exactly one dot in the whole filename, or just in the part before the extension?
Should the extension comparison be case-sensitive (e.g. is "TXT" valid)?
Can the substring before the dot contain digits or special characters, as long as it starts with a letter?
What should happen if the filename is empty or has no dot at all?
Should leading/trailing whitespace be considered part of the filename?
Are Unicode/non-ASCII letters allowed as the starting character before the dot?
answers: No, 'sound' is exactly equivalent to 'valid' — only the four listed conditions matter, no implicit extra requirements.
Anywhere in the whole filename, including the extension.
Exactly one dot in the whole filename.
Yes, case-sensitive — only exact lowercase matches from the list.
Yes, digits and other characters are fine before the dot as long as it starts with a letter.
Not specified beyond what's given; assume no whitespace is expected.
No, only the Latin alphabet a-z/A-Z.
